standard_prerequisites: The one-sided classical sequent calculus G3c: atomic axioms of the form C on the left and C on the right with everything else in the contexts, the propositional rules for not, and, or, and implies, and the notion of the height of a proof.
The induction-with-varying-contexts convention: in height-preserving arguments the inductive hypothesis is stated for all contexts, not just the ones occurring in the given proof.
core_obligations: State and prove the eight-part inversion lemma: each propositional rule of G3c is height-preserving invertible, so a proof of the conclusion sequent of height n yields proofs of each premise sequent of height at most n.

Carry out the full three-branch induction for the left-and rule: the axiom branch (atomic axioms cannot contain the principal formula, so the inverted sequent is again an axiom), the principal branch (the premise is exactly the inverted sequent), and the non-principal branch (apply the inductive hypothesis to the immediate subproofs and re-apply the last rule, with the max-formula height bookkeeping).
proof_roadmap: Prove the left-and inversion completely as the pattern case, with explicit derivations for the non-principal instance where the last rule is left-implies.

The remaining seven parts are instances of the same three-branch argument: for each rule the axiom branch is atomicity of axioms, the principal branch is immediate, and the non-principal branch is the inductive hypothesis plus re-application of the last rule, so the height bound is preserved by the max formula.
difficulty_reason: A methodical three-branch induction with explicit proof-tree derivations and height bookkeeping; the substantive content is the varying-context inductive hypothesis and the axiom atomicity observation, each branch being a reader-verifiable construction.
